purpose: Teach: 対人/竹下/地主/産ん/取り出す/昌/キツイ/岬

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは対人交渉を大事にされた
lines.en: You know, dear, when I was young, my father set great store by dealing with people face to face.
lines.style: Slow reminiscing baritone, a long pause before naming his father, gaze somewhere far away.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、竹下登総理の時代を経験されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes — and you lived through Prime Minister Noboru Takeshita's day when you were young, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Gentle papery warmth, a slight wobble on the memory, rising softly into the question.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんの実家は地主だった
lines.en: Back then, dear, my father's family were landowners, you know.
lines.style: Measured and quiet, a small dry pride surfacing and then tucked politely away.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、子供を産んで育てる事を最優先にされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: In those days, having children and raising them well came before everything else, didn't it, dear?
lines.style: Soft remembering smile in the voice, slow affectionate cadence, the question barely a question.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが大事な茶器を取り出す時、慎重だった
lines.en: And when my father took out his treasured tea things, dear, he was so very careful with them.
lines.style: Hushed reverence, pace slowing as if his own hands were holding the cups.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、お友達の昌さんと付き合いがあったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you kept company with your friend Sho back in those days, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Warm coaxing lilt, fond emphasis on the old friend's name, gently trailing question.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは「戦後はキツイ時代だった」と仰った
lines.en: My father used to say it, dear — the postwar years were a hard, hard time.
lines.style: Voice dropping lower and slower, weight settling on the word hard, a long exhale after.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、岬の灯台守の方々と親しかったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you were close with the lighthouse keepers out on the cape, weren't you, dear?
lines.style: Bright soft closing warmth, the memory lifting her pitch, a tender settle at the end.
